content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 168.20, 134.30, 131.90, 128.20, 128.20, 127.40, 127.40 ppm.

Carbonyl carbons typically appear around 160-220 ppm (for ketones, aldehydes, esters, acids). The shift at 168.20 likely corresponds to a carbonyl carbon (maybe an ester or amide). Others are aromatic region (~120-140). So likely one carbonyl.

But need to be sure: Could there be more carbonyls hidden? Only one shift in carbonyl region. So answer 1.

We could also check IR for C=O stretch, but carbon NMR already indicates one carbonyl. Use IR to confirm presence of C=O band.
